notes:
A --mechanisms-only run: the execution and isolation mechanisms exercised without the lifecycle walk. The six not-run probes are the walk's -- subagent briefing, attribution, execution mode -- and are unmeasured here by construction rather than by failure. This run is not a certification and cannot become one; it is the decisive half, run cheaply.

Four probes pass here that had never passed in any run.

task-binding-recorded and task-completion-is-gated: TaskCreated bound a native task to the graph, and TaskCompleted fired with the completion gate evaluating the definition of done -- 1 allowed, 0 blocked. These were recorded as unreachable for two releases on the belief that a headless session had no task tools. The tools are gated by the model, not the mode, and CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1 reaches them.

background-execution-was-actually-dispatched: job 96c3ef5b ran and wrote its artifact while the platform still listed it as `working`. The previous probe rule would have called that 'the platform never ran it'; the corrected rule reads produced work as work, whatever the poll caught.

worktree-isolation-was-actually-used: two worktrees created, WorktreeCreate fired.

worktree-work-was-integrated-not-just-isolated fails, and the failure is the real finding. The repository shows one commit -- the shipped baseline -- and src/retention/policy.py modified in the working tree. That is an agent editing the main checkout directly, which is the opposite of integrating out of a worktree, and the earlier version of this probe would have accepted it as integration. No worktree was removed either. Isolation is created and never completed.

Teams remain unreachable: no CLI surface exists in 2.1.252, and the session asked to start one said so itself -- enabling the flag 'fixes the declaration, not the capability'.

CORRECTION, 2026-09-04. Any `worktree-isolation-was-actually-used` pass in this record is FALSE. The probe counted `worktree_created` events, and those events fired whether or not a worktree existed: WorktreeCreate is a provider hook, so this plugin's recorder was replacing the platform's creation with a script that recorded an event and made nothing. Every such event carries `path: null`. Proven by controlled experiment -- removing the registration and changing nothing else produced a real worktree. The probe now reads `git worktree list`. The verdict in this file stands as produced; certification was refused in every one of these runs regardless, so no verdict changes.
